data.text: COACH: validation evidence collected. Validator spawning next.

REJECTED: --delete-volumes regression. Commit c9c09d3ac deleted the upstream flag registration 'cmd.Flags().BoolVar(&c.deleteVolumes, \delete-volumes\, ...)' in internal/cli/down.go (introduced upstream in tilt-dev/tilt #6594, carried on master), replacing it with --worktrees. Consequences: (1) 'tilt down --delete-volumes' now fails with 'unknown flag' (reproduced on a fresh binary built from the worktree: exit=1); (2) the down help text still tells users 'Use --delete-volumes to change that' while the flag no longer exists; (3) c.deleteVolumes still exists and is passed to dcc.Down, now permanently false — docker-compose volumes can no longer be deleted at all. Plan §9.1 spec does not authorize removing this flag; --worktrees and --delete-volumes must coexist. Everything else in the task is sound: all 4 new TestDown* tests pass, all 13 pre-existing TestDown* tests pass, full internal/controllers/core/kubernetesapply package passes incl. 3 new GC tests (TestWorktreeGCClonesOrphanedClones, TestWorktreeGCKeepsLiveAndForeignClones, TestWorktreeGC_NoWorktreesNoop), clone-GC design matches plan §9.1, and the TestEdit hang in internal/cli is pre-existing (reproduces identically on master c9a44c7ec; get_test.go unchanged from baseline). Evidence: .agents/match/validations/tk-hd5-delete-volumes-regression.txt, .agents/match/validations/tk-hd5-final-validation.txt (commit 91a1890d3). Fix: restore the 'delete-volumes' flag registration in newDownCmd() (keep the new --worktrees flag alongside it); optionally add a test asserting both flags parse.
